title: Writer Introduction
content: Jawaharlal Nehru was born on November 14, 1889, in Allahabad to a Kashmiri Pandit family. His parents were Motilal Nehru and Swaroop Rani. He received his education at Harrow Public School in London and Trinity College, Cambridge. He was one of the foremost leaders of the Indian freedom struggle and served as the first Prime Minister of independent India.

title: Writer's Literary Background
content: Nehru was a prolific writer in English who contributed significantly to historical and autobiographical literature. His notable literary works include The Discovery of India, Glimpses of World History, and his autobiography Toward Freedom. His writings reflect his deep intellect, historical vision, and passion for building a modern, progressive nation.

title: Writer's View and Purpose of Writing
content: Through this historic speech, Nehru aimed to inspire the newly liberated citizens of India. His purpose was to remind the nation of its long struggle, the responsibilities that accompany freedom, and the sacred pledge to serve millions of suffering people. He wanted to unite diverse groups and instill faith in the future of democratic India.

title: Chapter Introduction
content: Tryst with Destiny is the full text of the historic speech delivered by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru to the Constituent Assembly on the midnight of August 14-15, 1947. It marks India's transition from foreign subjugation to independence. The chapter captures the solemnity, joy, and immense responsibilities of the birth of a free nation.

title: Story Narration
content: On the midnight of August 14-1947, as the world slept, India awoke to life and freedom after centuries of suppression. Jawaharlal Nehru addressed the Constituent Assembly, reminding everyone of the historic pledge made long ago. He paid homage to Mahatma Gandhi and freedom fighters, acknowledged the pain of partition, and urged citizens to work hard to eradicate poverty, disease, and ignorance to build a prosperous democratic nation.

title: Paragraph-wise Explanation Part 1
content: Nehru begins by recalling the long-standing pledge made by India for freedom. As the midnight hour strikes, India steps out from the old era into a new one. He emphasizes that this solemn moment demands complete dedication to the service of India, her people, and the larger cause of humanity, marking the end of past misfortunes.

title: Paragraph-wise Explanation Part 2
content: The author notes that freedom and power bring heavy responsibilities which rest upon the Constituent Assembly. Although the nation endured severe pains during partition, the past is over and the future beckons. This future requires incessant hard work to fulfill dreams of ending poverty, ignorance, disease, and inequality of opportunity across the world.

title: Paragraph-wise Explanation Part 3
content: Nehru appeals to the people of India to join this great adventure with faith and confidence, avoiding petty criticism. He honors Mahatma Gandhi, the architect of freedom who held aloft its torch. He remembers unknown soldiers and expresses solidarity with brothers and sisters separated by political boundaries, vowing to build a progressive, secular, and democratic nation.

title: Difficult English Words with Odia Meaning
content: Tryst means a meeting (सꥥꥶ). Destiny means fate (꥟ꥬꥧ). Redeem means to fulfill a promise (꥟ꥶꥡꥯꥧ ꥥꥧꥡꥥꥧ). Pledge means a vow or promise (ꥤꥥꥲꥡ). Incessant means unending or continuous (꥕ꥥꥣꥡꥧꥮꥯꥧ). Sovereign means supreme authority (ꥰꥥꥨꥪ꥟ꥯꥧ).

title: New Vocabulary
content: Conscience refers to an inner sense of right and wrong. Communalism refers to allegiance to one's own religious group rather than to the wider society. Endeavour means an earnest attempt or effort. Materializes means becomes a reality or actualizes. Fateful means having far-reaching consequences or highly significant.

title: Important Sentences and their Explanation
content: At the stroke of the midnight hour, when the world sleeps, India will awake to life and freedom. This sentence highlights the dramatic timing of India's independence when other nations were resting. Another key line, The ambition of the greatest man of our generation has been to wipe every tear from every eye, reflects Gandhian ideals of service to the poor.

title: Characters
content: Though not a traditional story with fictional characters, the speech features prominent historical figures. Mahatma Gandhi is central as the Father of the Nation and architect of freedom. The members of the Constituent Assembly represent the sovereign people of India, while the common citizens, peasants, and workers form the bedrock of the new nation.

title: Character Sketch of Mahatma Gandhi
content: Mahatma Gandhi is depicted as the supreme architect of Indian freedom. He embodied the ancient spirit of India, holding aloft the torch of freedom during dark times. Nehru praises him as magnificent in his faith, strength, courage, and humility, leaving an indelible imprint on the hearts of succeeding generations.

title: Plot Summary
content: The text outlines India's historic journey from colonial subjugation to independence. It traces the nation's unending quest, acknowledges the sorrow of Partition, honors freedom fighters, and lays down a futuristic roadmap. The narrative concludes with a renewed pledge to eradicate social evils and cooperate globally for peace and democracy.

title: Sequence of Events
content: First, India reaches the midnight hour of August 14-1947, waking up to freedom. Second, Nehru addresses the Constituent Assembly, taking a pledge of dedication. Third, he honors Mahatma Gandhi and remembers partition victims. Fourth, he outlines future duties toward the common man and sends greetings of peace to the world.

title: Central Idea
content: The central idea revolves around the realization of freedom and the heavy responsibilities it entails. Independence is not an endpoint but an opening of opportunities. Freedom requires relentless hard work, national unity, secularism, and dedication to uplift the poor and wipe every tear from every eye.

title: Theme
content: Key themes include freedom, national responsibility, democracy, secularism, and international peace. Nehru stresses that peace, freedom, and prosperity are indivisible in a globally connected world. He strongly denounces communalism and narrow-mindedness, promoting equality and justice for all citizens regardless of religion.

title: Moral of the Story
content: The moral is that freedom demands constant vigilance, discipline, and hard work rather than mere celebration. Citizens must shed petty differences, avoid destructive criticism, and unite to build a progressive nation. True freedom is achieved only when poverty, ignorance, and inequality are completely eradicated.

title: Tone and Mood
content: The tone of the speech is solemn, inspirational, visionary, and deeply patriotic. The mood shifts from reflective remembrance of past struggles and sorrows to high optimism, enthusiasm, and resolute determination for future nation-building.

title: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
content: Nehru employs powerful metaphors and symbolism throughout his speech. The star of freedom in the East and the torch of freedom symbolize hope and guidance. The phrase ox of a man or noble mansion of free India uses imagery and personification to convey grand architectural and moral concepts.

title: Grammar Points
content: The text extensively uses relative clauses introduced by pronouns like when, where, and who to add descriptive detail. For instance, At the stroke of the midnight hour, when the world sleeps uses an adverb clause of time. Negative prefixes like in-, im-, un-, and dis- are also key grammatical components discussed in the chapter.

title: Important Exam Points
content: Students must remember the exact date and time of the speech: midnight of August 14-1947. Key questions often focus on the pledge to be redeemed, the definition of India's unending quest, and Nehru's tribute to Mahatma Gandhi. The definition of the common man's upliftment and opposition to communalism are frequent board exam topics.

title: Complete Chapter Summary
content: Tryst with Destiny is an immortal speech by Jawaharlal Nehru welcoming India's independence. Marking the end of an era of suppression, Nehru reminds Indians of their unfulfilled pledges. He emphasizes eradicating poverty, disease, and ignorance. Paying tribute to Gandhi and martyrs, he urges unity, hard work, and global cooperation for permanent peace and democracy.

title: Chapter Conclusion
content: Nehru's speech concludes with an inspiring call to action and a reverent homage to the motherland. By shouting Jai Hind, he binds every Indian citizen, regardless of religion, to the sacred duty of service. The speech remains an enduring beacon of democratic values, national integration, and progressive vision for modern India.

title: 10 Very Short Questions with Answers
content: 1. When did India make her tryst with destiny? Ans: Long years ago before August 15, 1947. 2. Who delivered the speech Tryst with Destiny? Ans: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru. 3. What is the occasion of the speech? Ans: India's attainment of independence at midnight. 4. Who is referred to as the architect of freedom? Ans: Mahatma Gandhi. 5. What brings responsibility according to Nehru? Ans: Freedom and power. 6. What did Nehru call the greatest man of our generation? Ans: Mahatma Gandhi. 7. What must we avoid to build a great nation? Ans: Communalism and narrow-mindedness. 8. What phrase describes India's struggle? Ans: Unending quest. 9. What is said to be indivisible along with freedom? Ans: Peace and prosperity. 10. How does the speech conclude? Ans: With the slogan Jai Hind.

title: 10 Short Questions with Answers
content: 1. What does Nehru mean by India waking to life and freedom? Ans: He means India is emerging from colonial slavery into an era of self-rule and sovereign existence. 2. What kind of future does Nehru envision for India? Ans: A future of incessant striving to fulfill pledges and eradicate poverty, ignorance, and disease. 3. Why does Nehru mention the brothers and sisters across the border? Ans: He refers to people cut off by political boundaries during partition, emphasizing shared bonds. 4. What was the ambition of Mahatma Gandhi mentioned in the speech? Ans: To wipe every tear from every eye. 5. Why does Nehru state that there is no time for petty criticism? Ans: Because nation-building requires unity, faith, and confidence rather than division. 6. What role does the Constituent Assembly play? Ans: It is a sovereign body representing the people, bearing the heavy responsibility of governance. 7. What does Nehru say about the past sufferings? Ans: The past is over, and though hearts are heavy with Partition sorrows, the future beckons. 8. How should the people of India face freedom? Ans: In the spirit of a free and disciplined people, ready to shoulder burdens. 9. What is our duty towards the motherland? Ans: To pay reverent homage and bind ourselves afresh to her service. 10. Why cannot any nation be great if its people are narrow? Ans: Because narrowness in thought or action prevents true national greatness and unity.

title: 10 Long Board-style Questions with Detailed Answers
content: 1. Discuss the main significance and core message of Nehru's speech Tryst with Destiny. Ans: Nehru's speech marks the historic birth of independent India. Its core message is that freedom brings immense responsibility. Citizens must work tirelessly to eradicate poverty, ignorance, disease, and inequality, ensuring dignity for all. 2. How does Jawaharlal Nehru pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi in his speech? Ans: Nehru honors Gandhi as the architect of freedom who held aloft the torch during dark times. He praises his faith, strength, courage, and humility, urging future generations to keep his message alive. 3. What are the major challenges ahead of independent India as outlined by Nehru? Ans: The major challenges include ending poverty, disease, ignorance, and inequality of opportunity, healing partition wounds, and maintaining national unity against communalism. 4. Explain Nehru's vision of internationalism and global peace in the speech. Ans: Nehru believed dreams are for the world too, as nations are closely knit. He stated that peace, freedom, and prosperity are indivisible, pledging cooperation with all nations. 5. Why does Nehru strongly condemn communalism and narrow-mindedness? Ans: He condemns them because no nation can be great whose people are narrow in thought or action. All Indians have equal rights and obligations regardless of religion. 6. Describe the emotional tone of the nation at the midnight hour as depicted in the speech. Ans: The nation experienced joy mixed with sorrow due to partition traumas and Gandhi's absence, yet felt an overwhelming sense of hope and awakening. 7. What does Nehru mean by India's unending quest? Ans: It refers to India's historical journey from the dawn of civilization, marked by triumphs, failures, grandeur, and an unyielding pursuit of ideals. 8. What responsibilities does freedom impose on the citizens and leaders of India? Ans: Freedom requires hard work, discipline, rejection of petty criticism, and dedication to building a prosperous, democratic, and progressive society. 9. How does Nehru address the partition and those separated by political boundaries? Ans: He expresses sorrow for brothers and sisters cut off by political borders, assuring them that they remain part of India and share its fortunes. 10. Summarize the concluding appeal made by Nehru to the people of India. Ans: Nehru appeals to citizens to join the great adventure with faith, avoid communalism, uphold the honor of the motherland, and work relentlessly until pledges are fulfilled.
